title: fix(plugin-form): give each MasterDetail entry its own identity and resolution status
body:
Fixes #6372 Fixes #6371 Both cards change the **per-entry shape of the same resolver**, so they land as one shape. `resolvedDetails` was a plain `MasterDetailDetailConfig[]` carrying no per-entry metadata, so both *what happened to this entry* (#6372) and *which entry is this* (#6371) were inferred from the entry's **position in the array**. One per-entry record answers both — landing them separately would have meant two independent reshapes, the second rewriting the first. ```ts interface DetailEntry { id: string; // synthesized once from the incoming config → #6371 config: MasterDetailDetailConfig; status: 'pending' | 'declined' | 'ready' | 'failed'; // → #6372 } ``` Scope is `packages/plugin-form/src/MasterDetailForm.tsx` and its tests. `LineItemsPanel.tsx`, `deriveMasterDetail.ts` and `packages/spec` are untouched. --- ## What discharges #6372 — per-entry resolution status **Premise measured, not inherited.** The card says of itself that it is a source read. Driven at runtime against unmodified `origin/main` @ `631d81dbf`, a detail whose `getObjectSchema` **rejects** renders exactly: ```html

PO lines

Loading columns…

``` The premise holds. That message is permanent: the fetch is not retried, so nothing can ever replace it. **The fix.** Entries carry a resolution status — the smallest shape that tells *failed* from *in flight*, which on the old shape were identical (both simply have no `columns`). A failed entry renders a distinct refusal placeholder naming the child object, on the `AdvancedChartImpl` precedent (`role="status"` — a refusal is a state, not an alert). The previously-discarded error is logged, with the error object passed through so the stack survives; the parity bar is the `!childObject` decline arm, which has warned since #5940. ⭐ **The `try` covered two different failures, and this PR separates them.** The single bare `catch` wrapped both `await getObjectSchema(...)` **and** `deriveDetail(...)`. Routing both into the new placeholder would make it state something false — a schema that loads fine and then yields no relationship field is a *configuration* error, not a load failure. So the fetch and the derive are caught separately: - **fetch throws** → `status: 'failed'` → refusal placeholder. #6372's subject. - **derive throws** → entry unchanged → still `Loading columns…`. **Render deliberately unchanged**: #6360 pinned this exact case (`detailChildObjectDecline.test.tsx`, *"still says Loading columns… while it resolves"*), and repointing it is a triage decision, not a rider here. Its error does stop being swallowed. Filed separately as a finding — see below. ## What discharges #6371 — per-entry synthesized identity ⛔ **Not a duplicate-key collision.** The map index is unique among siblings by construction, so two declined details keyed as `undefined-0` and `undefined-1` — distinct, no React warning, no remount collision. This PR starts from the **index-identity hazard**, as the card's correction requires. The real defect: for a declined entry the data half of `` `${d.childObject}-${i}` `` is `undefined`, leaving **position** as the entry's whole identity — and the row-state store was addressed the same way, seeded once at mount and never re-synced when the authored config changed. **Identity** is synthesized once from the incoming config, never from the map index: the child object for a named collection, and the **authored position in `rawDetails`** for a declined one, which has no other identity to offer. Row state is keyed by that id, so a collection can only ever read its own slot. ⭐ **Three position-associated reads, not the one the card names.** The dispatch order's census correction named two (`:226`, `:264`); a third turned up while re-deriving: | read | consequence on `origin/main` | |---|---| | `value={state[i]?.rows}` — the grid value | the collection showed another collection's rows | | `details.reduce((acc, d, i) => … state[i] …)` — **the subtotal reducer** | a reorder **mis-computed the document total** | | `details.filter(d => d.relationshipField).map((d, i) => stateRef.current[i])` — **the batch payload on save** | after the filter, `i` indexes the **filtered** array while the store is indexed against the **full** one, so a declined entry above a real collection shifted every read below it by one and that collection's rows were **silently dropped from the transaction** | The third is data loss on save, not a display defect. It is fixed here because the reshape forces it — the positional array it read no longer exists — and declining to convert it would mean deliberately reconstructing the bug. It is pinned by its own test and called out here so it can be reviewed on its own. --- ## Ghost-assertion guard — every new assertion measured failing first Both readings taken with the **final** test files. The failing reading restores `origin/main`'s `MasterDetailForm.tsx` under them (`git checkout $BASE -- `), with the mutation and the restore each confirmed by blob hash on disk, and `git diff HEAD` empty afterwards. **Against unmodified `origin/main` source — 6 failed | 5 passed (11)** | card | assertion | failure on `main` | |---|---|---| | #6372 | refusal placeholder for a thrown fetch | `Unable to find an element by: [data-testid="md-detail-schema-unavailable"]` | | #6372 | the discarded error is logged naming the object | `expected null not to be null` | | #6372 | the **derive** error is logged (render half unchanged) | `expected the derive failure to be logged, not discarded: expected undefined to be truthy` | | #6371 | rows stay with their own collection across a **reorder** | `expected '' to be '100'` | | #6371 | rows + subtotal stay with their own collection across a **removal** | `expected '' to be '250'` | | #6371 | each collection's own rows reach the **batch** | `expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0` | **With the fix — 15 passed (15)** across the two new files *and* `MasterDetailForm.detailChildObjectDecline.test.tsx`, whose four #6360 assertions are untouched. ⚠️ **The guard caught a ghost in my own test and it was rewritten.** The first draft asserted the post-reorder grid value inside a plain `waitFor`. `resolvedDetails` still holds the **previous** array when `rerender` returns — the resolve effect is async — so `waitFor`'s first synchronous attempt read the **pre-reorder** DOM and **passed against unmodified `main`**, where the settled DOM in fact shows an empty grid. The tests now block on a DOM-order gate (`waitForDeclinedSectionsBefore`) that can only become true once the new config has landed. Probe on `main` after settling: `cellCount=1 values=[""] · subtotal=¥0.00 · sameSection=false`. **Degenerate controls** (green on `main` *and* after, so the new behaviour is attributable to the failure/decline rather than a blanket change): - a detail whose fetch **succeeds and resolves** → renders its grid, no placeholder, no `Loading columns…` - a detail still **in flight** → keeps `Loading columns…`, which is TRUE there - #6360's config hint still owns the `!childObject` arm - a **resolved** detail with no declined sibling → untouched - a rerender that **moves nothing** → no remount, rows intact --- ## Checks Union run on `0a3d1d8cc` — the head of this branch, after merging `origin/main`. | check | verdict line | |---|---| | `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-form type-check` | `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` → `TYPECHECK_EXIT=0` | | `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-form lint` | `✖ 691 problems (0 errors, 691 warnings)` — warnings pre-existing, `LINT_EXIT=0` | | `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-form/` | `Test Files 69 passed (69)` · `Tests 685 passed (685)` | | `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` | `✅ check-control-bytes: OK (scanned 5270 tracked text file(s))` | | `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` | `✅ No changeset declares a major bump.` | `tsconfig.test.json` `--listFiles` confirms both new test files are compiled (2 hits), so the typecheck reading really covers them. Changeset: `.changeset/6372-6371-master-detail-entry-identity.md` — `patch`, `@object-ui/plugin-form`. ## Out of scope, filed separately - A schema that **loads** but yields no relationship field still shows a permanent `Loading columns…` — the same unbounded-wait shape one arm over. Its render is pinned by #6360, so changing it is a triage call. - `React does not recognize the previousValues prop on a DOM element` — a pre-existing warning from the parent `ObjectForm` surface, present on unmodified `main`. ⛔ Draft on purpose — the PM lands this.
